**AI 380: Human-AI Interaction · Willamette University**

A **codespace** is a ready-to-use Linux machine with VS Code, running in the cloud and attached to your GitHub repo.

- No installs on your laptop
- Docker and Python ready to go
- Everyone gets the same setup

## 🛠️ How to use this walkthrough

1. Read the concept.
2. Do the step in your browser.
3. Pass the checkpoint.
4. Continue only when it passes.

::: {.checkpoint}
**You need:** A GitHub account and the `project_name` repo already pushed to GitHub.
:::


## 📊 What Codespaces is good for

| Good for | Not good for |
|---|---|
| Labs and class demos | An always-on public website |
| Same environment for every student | Anything that must keep running overnight |
| Running Docker and Rasa without local installs | Large, long jobs that burn your free hours |
| Trying the game over HTTPS (microphone works) | Serving the grader a link days later |

> A codespace **stops when idle**. For a site that must stay online, use a host from the Azure workshop.

## 💰 Free allowance

| Resource | Free personal allowance (approx.) |
|---|---|
| Compute | About **120 core hours** per month |
| Storage | About **15 GB-months** per month |

- Core hours scale with machine size: a **2-core** machine gives about **60 hours**, a **4-core** about 30.
- Idle codespaces stop after **30 minutes** by default.
- Check GitHub's current limits before class; they change.

## 🚀 Part 1 · Create a codespace

1. Open your `project` repo on github.com.
2. Click the green **Code** button.
3. Choose the **Codespaces** tab.
4. Click **Create codespace on main**.

A new browser tab opens and builds the environment. The first build takes a few minutes.

## 🧭 Part 1 · Find your way around

| Area | What it is |
|---|---|
| **Explorer** (left) | Your repo files |
| **Editor** (center) | Edit code like in desktop VS Code |
| **Terminal** (bottom) | A Linux shell inside the cloud machine |
| **Ports** tab (bottom) | Web servers running in the codespace |
| **Bottom-left badge** | Codespace name; click for stop and rebuild options |

## ✅ Part 1 · Check the tools

In the terminal:

```bash
docker --version
python --version
git status
```

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 1:** All three commands run. If `docker` is missing, continue to Part 2; the dev container fixes it.
:::

## ② Make it repeatable {.section-slide background-color="#263b4e"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Part 2 · Dev container and secrets
:::

**One file tells every student's codespace what to install**

## 🧱 Part 2 · The dev container

A **dev container** is a description of the environment, stored in the repo. Create:

```text
Calm_Wordle/
└── .devcontainer/
    └── devcontainer.json
```

Anyone who opens the repo in a codespace gets the same Python version, Docker, extensions, and ports.

## 📝 `devcontainer.json` · Game and Docker

```json
{
  "name": "Calm_Wordle",
  "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:1-3.12-bookworm",
  "features": {
    "ghcr.io/devcontainers/features/docker-in-docker:2": {}
  },
  "forwardPorts": [8000, 5005],
  "portsAttributes": {
    "8000": { "label": "Game" },
    "5005": { "label": "Rasa" }
  },
  "customizations": {
    "vscode": { "extensions": ["ms-python.python", "ms-azuretools.vscode-docker"] }
  }
}
```

## 🔍 Read it line by line

| Key | Why |
|---|---|
| `image` | Python 3.12 base with developer tools |
| `docker-in-docker` | Lets you run `docker build` and `docker compose` inside the codespace |
| `forwardPorts` | Ports to expose to your browser |
| `portsAttributes` | Friendly names in the **Ports** tab |
| `extensions` | VS Code add-ons installed automatically |

## 🔄 Apply the change

1. Commit and push `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`.
2. In the codespace, press `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + P`.
3. Run **Codespaces: Rebuild Container**.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 2:** After the rebuild, `docker --version` works and the Ports tab lists *Game* and *Rasa*.
:::

## 🔐 Part 2 · Secrets, never in the repo

Rasa Pro needs `RASA_LICENSE`. Voice needs `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`. Store them as **Codespaces secrets**:

1. github.com → profile photo → **Settings**.
2. **Codespaces → New secret**.
3. Name: `RASA_LICENSE`. Paste the value.
4. **Repository access:** select only `Calm_Wordle`.
5. Repeat for `DEEPGRAM_API_KEY`.

Secrets appear as environment variables in new or rebuilt codespaces. **Do not commit `.env`.**

## 🔎 Check the secret is loaded

```bash
test -n "$RASA_LICENSE" && echo "license set" || echo "license missing"
```

Prints a word, not the key itself.

> Never `echo` the key and never paste it into chat, screenshots, or commits.

## ③ Run the project {.section-slide background-color="#a93632"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Part 3 · Game, ports, Rasa
:::

**Start → forward → open → test**

## 🎮 Part 3 · Run the game

Either run Python directly:

```bash
HOST=0.0.0.0 PORT=8000 python web_server.py
```

or run the same Docker image you built for Azure:

```bash
docker build -t calm-wordle .
docker run --rm -p 8000:8000 calm-wordle
```

Codespaces notices the port and shows a **notification**.

## 🌐 Part 3 · Open a forwarded port

1. Open the **Ports** tab.
2. Find **8000 · Game**.
3. Click the globe icon, or hover and choose **Open in Browser**.

The address looks like:

```text
https://<codespace-name>-8000.app.github.dev
```

It is **HTTPS**, so the microphone works without Caddy or a certificate.

## 🔒 Port visibility

| Setting | Who can open it |
|---|---|
| **Private** (default) | Only you, signed in to GitHub |
| **Organization** | Members of your GitHub organization |
| **Public** | Anyone with the link |

> Make a port **Public** only for a short demo. Never make Rasa's port 5005 public: anyone with the link could use your API keys.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 3:** The game loads at the forwarded HTTPS address and the microphone prompt appears.
:::

## 🤖 Part 3 · Run Rasa in the codespace

Rasa Pro needs more memory than a 2-core machine may have for training. Change the size first:

1. Command palette: **Codespaces: Change Machine Type**.
2. Choose **4-core** (or larger if available).
3. Wait for the restart.

Then, from your Rasa project folder:

```bash
rasa train
rasa inspect
```

Forwarded port **5005** shows the Inspector in your browser.

## 🎙️ Part 3 · Voice test

```bash
export DEEPGRAM_API_KEY=...   # or set it as a Codespaces secret
rasa inspect
```

- Open the forwarded Rasa URL.
- Allow microphone access.
- Say: **"I want to learn the medication reminder."**

::: {.notes}
Prefer the Codespaces secret over exporting a key in a shell, so the key is not in shell history.
:::

## ④ Save hours and wrap up {.section-slide background-color="#0067b8"}

::: {.eyebrow}
Part 4 · Cost, cleanup, troubleshooting
:::

**Stop → delete → reuse**

## ⏱️ Part 4 · Protect your free hours

1. **Stop** when done: command palette → **Codespaces: Stop Current Codespace**.
2. Closing the browser tab does **not** stop it; it stops after the idle timeout.
3. Choose the **smallest machine** that works. Use 4-core only for Rasa training.
4. Check usage: github.com → **Settings → Billing and plans**.
5. Set a spending limit of **$0** so you cannot be charged beyond the free allowance.

## 🗑️ Part 4 · Delete old codespaces

Stopped codespaces still use **storage**.

- Open <https://github.com/codespaces>.
- Use the `...` menu next to each codespace and choose **Delete**.

Commit and push anything you need **before** deleting. Files not pushed are lost.

::: {.checkpoint}
**Checkpoint 4:** Your work is pushed, the codespace is stopped, and you can find the usage page.
:::

## 🧯 Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause → Fix |
|---|---|
| `docker: command not found` | No Docker feature → add `docker-in-docker`, rebuild container |
| Port does not appear in the Ports tab | Server bound to `127.0.0.1` only or not running → start with `HOST=0.0.0.0` and check the terminal |
| Page asks you to sign in to GitHub | Port is Private → open it from the Ports tab while signed in, or change visibility briefly |
| Rasa training killed or very slow | Out of memory → change machine type to 4-core or larger |
| Secret is missing | Added after the codespace was created → rebuild or create a new codespace |
| Microphone blocked | Not using the forwarded `https://` URL → open from the Ports tab |
| "Out of free hours" notice | Quota used → stop codespaces, wait for the monthly reset |

## 🆚 Codespaces vs. a hosted site

| Question | Codespaces | Azure VM / Render |
|---|---|---|
| Setup effort | Lowest | Higher |
| Always on | No | Yes |
| Good for the grader to visit later | No | Yes |
| Good for lab and Rasa experiments | **Yes** | Yes |
| Cost to student | Free allowance | Student credit or paid tier |

## 🛡️ Safety checklist

- [ ] Secrets are Codespaces secrets, not files in the repo
- [ ] `.env`, `models/`, and `saved_games.json` stay in `.gitignore`
- [ ] Rasa port 5005 is **Private**
- [ ] The codespace is stopped when you leave
- [ ] Work is committed and pushed

## 📇 Quick reference

| Task | How |
|---|---|
| Create | Repo → **Code → Codespaces → Create** |
| Command palette | `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + P` |
| Rebuild | **Codespaces: Rebuild Container** |
| Change size | **Codespaces: Change Machine Type** |
| Stop | **Codespaces: Stop Current Codespace** |
| Manage all | <https://github.com/codespaces> |

Submit:

1. A screenshot of the **Ports** tab with the Game port forwarded.
2. A screenshot of the game running at the `app.github.dev` address.
3. Your `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`.
4. A short note: **one limitation of Codespaces compared with Azure.**

> A cloud dev environment is for building and testing, not for hosting.
